bounds: Two selection calls, three conversation identities plus null, five symbolic draft values including empty and one unsaved initial edit. No active send or queued attachment. Cold no-cache loads project successful history to one user row. Loader-owned 404 fallback, cache/overlay internals, mounted React effects and final message-anchor application are unmodeled. Each missing-result branch isolates the outer callback interface. Each call has at most one primary and one recovery load; no counter wraps.

assumptions: Weak fairness of primary success, empty list completion and recovery success for each pending call. These actions model host operations that eventually settle. Two finite calls prevent perpetual supersession.
This outer callback completion does not establish message-anchor success, notification receipt, request dequeue, or progress when a provider promise never settles.
The source callback has no surface-mounted predicate. Unmount leaves the shared selection epoch current, so failure can restore the previous selection and publish a notice.
Each per-call unmount is an over-approximation of the actual overlay lifetime, which may retire multiple calls together. The one-call counterexample matches the real callback probe.

The retired-write witness never clears. An eventual suffix without that witness is equivalent to avoiding the bad event, and its violation includes a loop. The real mounted callback test independently observes the write.
